Thanks Sara — looping internal ops and pricing to make sure we present clean options. Copying Jordan (deal ops), Irene (legal/procurement SLAs), and Naomi (partner ops).

Quick summary of the ask: ACME wants Marketplace invoicing to go to procurement@acme.com and ResellerX expects a separate pass-through for their margin. Two options we usually present:

Option A — Separate reseller SKU (recommended when partner needs line-of-sight on revenue and to simplify partner payouts). Pro: clear audit trail for reseller; Con: more SKUs to map and potential AWS listing complexity.

Option B — Embed partner margin in list price and pay partner off-invoice (simpler for Marketplace listing, less line-item noise). Pro: simpler SKU set; Con: partner loses visibility and requires reconciliation for payouts.

Jordan / Naomi — can you suggest the preferred routing and the typical percent splits you see for a reseller + regional broker? Also, confirm any restrictions from AWS on multiple invoice lines for private offers that might block Option A.

Irene — if we go Option A (separate SKU), do we need any additional language in the private offer terms to handle tax and rev recognition?

Thanks — I'll prepare a brief comparison and a sample invoice waterfall once you confirm.

Elliot — quick ops read from pricing/marketplace side.

Short answers: AWS Marketplace supports multiple line items in a private offer, but seller-managed pass-throughs are easier to reconcile if the partner receives their margin as a separate SKU/line item. That said, some partners prefer to stay off the invoice and receive settlements outside Marketplace.

Suggested runbook for ACME (based on similar deals):

1) Invoice routing: Configure Marketplace private offer so invoice is issued to procurement@acme.com with a PDF copy to finance@acme.com. Use billing address as provided in the attachment.

2) Reseller margin split: introduce a "Partner Pass-Through" SKU representing ResellerX margin. Typical split for enterprise deals we see: 12-18% reseller fee (ResellerX) + 3-6% regional broker fee if a secondary distributor is involved. For ACME I would propose 15% reseller + 5% regional broker as a starting point.

3) SKU mapping: Create explicit SKUs for (A) Redwood usage, (B) Reseller pass-through, (C) Broker pass-through (if needed). This keeps marketplace telemetry clean and enables line-item visibility in ACME's GL.

4) Tax & rev recog: If pass-through SKUs are pure commissions (no fulfillment by partner), we recommend adding language to the private offer terms clarifying who is the seller of record for tax purposes. Irene — we'll need language to ensure Redwood recognizes revenue net of commission versus gross depending on partner role.

I've attached a draft invoice waterfall (internal) and an example price file formatted for AWS PO ingestion.

Attachments: Draft_Invoice_Waterfall.xlsx, AWS_PO_Pricefile_Template.csv

Happy to walk through with ACME this afternoon if helpful.

Thanks Jordan — this aligns with what legal needs to cover. A few asks from my side before we send to ACME for signature: 

1) Confirm seller of record and tax treatment: If ResellerX is only receiving a commission, Redwood remains seller of record. We'll add a clause clarifying this and that reseller commissions are paid separately by Redwood.

2) Line-item broker fee: ACME requested visibility on the broker fee. If we add a broker pass-through SKU we need to be explicit about pricing (fixed percent vs negotiated delta) and whether that SKU is refundable in the event of credits/SLA adjustments.

3) SLA credits & invoice adjustments: Procurement often wants invoice-level SLA crediting. Recommend adding a short SLA credit process in the terms and mapping how credits flow across SKUs.
